es_replikleri: You took the mother inside and left her lad out in the cold at the gate...
Did it behoove us to snap the very pillar of their hearth, my husband?

meslek_varyantlari.dokumaci: How shall I face the women at the loom tomorrow? They will speak only of that mother's wailing.
meslek_varyantlari.firinci: Do you believe bread bought with the tears of a broken family will taste sweet on our tongues?
meslek_varyantlari.ebe: This is like tearing a swaddled newborn from its mother's breast; my heart cannot bear it.

savunmak.metin: The law is clear, wife; for the security of our settlement, they had to be separated.

kabul_etmek.metin: You speak true... My senses were clouded in the biting wind at the gate; my soul aches.

susmak.metin: The gatekeeper remained silent beside the hearth, staring down at the glowing coals.

es_replikleri: You cornered him well when that traveler attempted to conceal his saddlebag.
His face paled when you threw his falsehood in his teeth; your eye at the gate is keen, husband.

meslek_varyantlari.dokumaci: You unraveled his knot deftly; like a master craftsman discerning flawed yarn.
meslek_varyantlari.firinci: Such scoundrels deserve no indulgence; let only honest folk enter, even if hungry.
meslek_varyantlari.ebe: A liar's pulse races fast; you said you could read it in his glance, and you were proven right.

savunmak.metin: In a frontier Beylik, the hearth of a lax sentry is swiftly extinguished.

kabul_etmek.metin: My eye was upon him, yet my heart takes no joy in catching men in shame.

susmak.metin: The gatekeeper nods slightly, gazing into the fire without pride.

tutulmayan_soz.baslik: A Broken Vow to the Villagers
es_replikleri: You promised charcoal to the blacksmith's apprentice, yet today diverted it to the barracks.
A gatekeeper's word is regarded as a bond in this settlement; if trust falters, we cannot endure.

meslek_varyantlari.dokumaci: The women at the well whisper among themselves that the master guard went back on his word.
meslek_varyantlari.firinci: A promise is like dough in the oven; if its hour passes, the loaf turns to stone.
meslek_varyantlari.ebe: Trust is like a living soul; once departed, it is grievous hard to recall.

savunmak.metin: Orders arrived from the Sanjak; of necessity I gave priority to the garrison.

kabul_etmek.metin: The fault is mine; come dawn, my first walk shall be to the smithy to ask forgiveness.

susmak.metin: With a pang of guilt, the gatekeeper wipes his sword scabbard and utters no word.

es_replikleri: You allowed that trooper hunted by the Sanjak subasi to slip into our settlement.
If enforcement cavalry ride up to our portal tomorrow, what account will you render?

meslek_varyantlari.dokumaci: A deserter must not draw near the looms; do not draw fire upon the village, husband.
meslek_varyantlari.firinci: A soldier belongs in his barracks; must we divide our bread with a fugitive?
meslek_varyantlari.ebe: If he is wounded we will bind his hurts, but if blood drips from his steel, he brings calamity.

savunmak.metin: He was a wretched trooper fleeing tyranny; besides, we desperately need men who can bear arms.

kabul_etmek.metin: I know full well the grave risk I took; to guard the village I will double the watch.

susmak.metin: The gatekeeper stares out through the window into the dark road, answering nothing.

es_replikleri: You took in that frail boy shivering upon the portal...
He is starving, his garments in tatters; to whose care shall we entrust this child?

meslek_varyantlari.dokumaci: Place him beside me, let him learn to spin wool; he will earn his keep.
meslek_varyantlari.firinci: Let us apprentice him to the bakery; he can knead dough and earn his daily bread.
meslek_varyantlari.ebe: Tender mercy is what that boy needs; let him drink a bowl of hot broth by the hearth.

savunmak.metin: I could not cast him into the snow, wife; to shield the orphan is the honor of the Beylik.

kabul_etmek.metin: Our cottage is small, but our hearts are spacious; a bowl of our broth is enough for him.

susmak.metin: The gatekeeper looks upon the carved wooden toy the boy brought, smiling gently.

es_replikleri: The gate was tranquil today, husband; praise be that no brawl or strife arose.
The mountain frost descended early; drink your soup while it is steaming.

meslek_varyantlari.dokumaci: Today we wove two bolts of wool felt; the village women were cheerful.
meslek_varyantlari.firinci: Our firewood is stacked, our flour blessed; the oven blazes warmly, praise be.
meslek_varyantlari.ebe: I dried the medicinal herbs; no grave ailment afflicts the settlement.

savunmak.metin: Serenity is a blessing, wife; yet on the watch one must never let down his guard.

kabul_etmek.metin: Praise be to God; so long as smoke rises from our chimney, it is enough.

susmak.metin: The gatekeeper cradles the warm bowl in both hands, resting in peaceful silence.

es_yangin_ve_goc.baslik: The Burning of the Old Village and Migration
es_replikleri: As the wind howls down the chimney, my mind wanders back to our old village torched by the Tekfur, my lord...
When our shoes tore to shreds in the mud, you gave me your own boots and your feet turned to ice.

savunmak.metin: Those days are past, wife; the ramparts of this village and my own chest are your shield.

kabul_etmek.metin: I too cannot forget that smoke; I keep vigilant guard on watch at all times.

susmak.metin: The sentry stirs the embers and holds his wife's hand tightly.

es_yetim_ve_cocuk.baslik: Orphans and the Longing for Children
es_replikleri: Whenever I look upon Turna and Dursun my heart weeps; three winters have passed yet our hearth lacks a child's laughter, my lord...
Hearing of infants perishing from plague in mountain hamlets, I sigh for our own destiny.

savunmak.metin: Turna and Dursun are our sacred trust now; so long as the hearth smokes, hope still lives.

kabul_etmek.metin: It is Heaven that bestows both sustenance and patience; in due time our home shall be joyful.

susmak.metin: The sentry bows his head, comforting his sorrow in silence by embracing his wife.

es_gece_sifasi.baslik: Spouse's Herbal Remedy on Frost Watch
es_replikleri: Rime has gathered upon your beard again, my lord; unbuckle your belt and drink this steaming linden and thyme brew.
The north wind has parched your lungs; it is living souls, not silver coins, that guard this village!

savunmak.metin: Bless your hands, wife; in this bitter cold it came like water of life.

kabul_etmek.metin: Pine honey is costly, yet life is precious; blessings upon you, wife.

susmak.metin: The sentry clasps the warm mug with both hands, breathing in the fragrant steam.

es_replikleri: I have filled our guest's bowl, husband; tonight let the hearth speak, not the gate.

misafir_dallari.varsayilan: Guest (%s): 'Your household is blessed; a warm bowl of stew kept us through the night.'
misafir_dallari.tanidik: Guest (%s): 'I passed your gate once before; I knew the smoke of your hearth from afar.'
misafir_dallari.hediye: Guest (%s): 'May kindness never go unreturned; I left a share from my pack for your home.'
misafir_dallari.hirsizlik: Guest (%s): 'The road is long and the night is frostbitten; I must be off before dawn.'

savunmak.metin: Even when bunks grow scarce at the gate, there is always room for one bowl at our table.

kabul_etmek.metin: Do not fret, wife; a guest comes with fortune and leaves with fortune.

susmak.metin: The sentry stirs the embers and nods quietly toward the guest.
